newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU needs more flexible grain export rules - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: EU needs more flexible grain export rules - ONIC.

text.p: France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday that the European Union needed more flexibility to use subsidies or taxes for its grain exports to respond to world price fluctuations.
ONIC's president Michel Marie said at a news conference that the office's permanent committee will set up a working group to review the issue before making a formal proposal.
EU exporters can bid to export grain on world markets through either a daily channel or the more rigid weekly grain auction system.
In the daily bidding system the EU can at any time modify the refund applying to exports.

On Monday for instance the EU scrapped the zero refund applying to daily soft wheat exports, replacing it with a nil value refund, that leaves exporters subject to a tax, should the EU decide to take such a step. The EU made the decision in the face of soaring world prices.
But if the EU wants to introduce taxes into the weekly auction channel that currently applies only to export subsidies, it needs to change EU regulations.
This is often a lenghthy process and this hinders exports in the meantime, ONIC officials said.

"To introduce taxes in the current free market auction, rules must be changed. This requires the EU grain comittee to vote and limits the system for a while," said said Michel Ferret, head of ONIC's international affairs division.

Michel Marie also criticised the current nil value refund applying to daily soft wheat exports, saying that it gave exporters no visibility to do business, placing them in what he called a "no man's land".
